raw_response:
I've been farming these 10.9 mu for 40 years, since I was 27. Never went to school, can't read the fertilizer bags, but I know every piece of this land. This year I'm 67, my knees hurt when it rains, but my sons and their wives are here to help — 8 of us total under one roof, so we have hands, thank heavens. Hiring workers costs cash and we don't have much to throw around.

I keep my land split five ways because you can't trust just one crop. Last year my neighbor Auntie Wang planted only cotton and the bollworms came, she lost half her income. I have 4 mu for wheat and then maize right after, 3 mu for cotton, 2 mu for millet for our own porridge and the chickens, and the remaining 1.9 mu by the house is stevia. The buyer comes every autumn for the stevia leaves. It's extra work but last year when the cotton price dropped, that stevia money bought the grandchildren their school clothes.

For the wheat, I plant around October 10th, same as always. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer for every 2 mu before sowing — that's how I count it, in bags, not in kilos — and then at jointing in spring if the wheat looks yellow I scatter a little urea by hand. I can't afford more. The shop man wants cash upfront now, no more credit. I irrigate three times: after planting if the soil is dry, then at jointing, then when the grain is filling. The well water costs money since they put meters on, so I don't water more than I have to. I expect about 400 jin per mu, same as most years if the frost doesn't come early.

The maize goes in right after we cut the wheat, usually around June 10th. The window is tight, maybe five or six days, we all work until dark. I don't till much, just open the furrow in the wheat stubble and drop the hybrid seed. I give it less fertilizer than the wheat — half a bag of compound for the 4 mu, and one more handful when it's knee-high. Water it twice if it's hot. Should get around 450 jin per mu. Last year my nephew helped for two days during the rush and I paid him 100 yuan each day and fed him dinner. I might need to do that again.

Cotton I plant after Qingming, around April 20th. It needs so many hands for picking, but my daughters-in-law do it between cooking and childcare. I put compound fertilizer in the rows before planting, about one bag for the 3 mu, and side-dress with urea when it flowers. I spray for weeds and for the bollworm — last year the worms were bad so I bought insecticide from the shop, it hurt my wallet but I had to. Two irrigations, maybe three if July is dry. I hope for 250 jin of lint per mu, but it depends on the rain and the pests.

The 2 mu of millet is for us, not for sale mostly. I spread some manure we saved from the pigs and a little bit of compound fertilizer, not much. I saved the seed from last year so it costs me nothing. Water it once, maybe twice. Millet doesn't complain much, it grows even when you're not looking.

The stevia plot is 1.9 mu near the house. I planted it three years ago and it comes back. The children help pick the leaves in July and August when the buyer calls. I give it a bit of compound fertilizer in spring and another handful after the first picking. Water twice. It's extra work but it's cash in hand, and at my age I need things that pay quickly.

I don't hire labor if I can help it — my family does everything. Total costs... seeds for the maize and cotton, fertilizer bags, pesticide, water electricity... I think about 3,000 yuan. That's already too much, but you can't farm without spending something. I'm not changing anything new this year. Last year was okay, not great, not terrible. When you're my age with no schooling, you don't try fancy new things — you do what kept your family fed for 40 years. If the stevia buyer pays a good price this autumn, maybe next year I'll buy one more bag of fertilizer for the wheat. But only if the children don't need the money first.
